pr_title: Execute async cleanup tasks in CoordinatorTests
pr_body:
Closing the `JoinValidationService` will enqueue a cache-cleaning task which must be executed to release any pages held by the cache.

This commit also introduces a deterministic leak detector to replace the one based on garbage collection, because in these tests we know exactly the expected lifecycle of all allocated pages.

Closes #91599
Closes #91379
Closes #90576
pr_comments: I'm running some iterations of the `CoordinatorTests` in the background to see if this causes any problems before merging it.

comments: Looks like the problem actually occured during `CoordinatorTests.testUnhealthyNodesGetsRemoved`, but only exhibited itself in the hashcode test
From the stack trace, the problem is somewhere in the coordinator, or around `JoinValidationService` -> Distributed
Looks like the same sort of thing as #89712. Still haven't been able to reproduce this locally despite many attempts.

I did spot some theoretically possible leaks when assertions are on around the cleanup code for `JoinValidationService.serializeClusterState`, but I would then expect an assertion failure from that test. Unless the AssertionError was getting swallowed by a thread handler or otherwise ignored somewhere else...

I don't think that explains it although you're right that we should fix it anyway - see https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/90597. This test is supposed to run (deterministically!) on the main test thread. , It's possible that one of the enclosing `finally` blocks might itself throw an exception which would overrule the `AssertionError` but there's nothing in the call stack that would completely swallow an exception AFAICT so _something_ should bubble up to the test runner and cause it to fail in that case.

review_comments:
It would be nice if log is e.g. TRACE to also capture the thread stack of the pages. That way, if the assertion that there is no page remaining fails, we may be able to inspect which thread stacks created them. I believe this should be cheap for the majority of the tests (since I guess they do not run in TRACE mode) and when a test fails we may easily re-run it with TRACE to figure out leaks.

This is optional if you consider this would be beneficial.

I think I'd prefer not to do this here, it would mean we can't just use a counter to check for leaks (or we'd have two whole different implementations depending on the log level). I'd rather just add such tracing code as and when it's needed.
